comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Narrowed 2026-10-05: a laptop tab holding only a zsh shell (p296he013e, made with muster tab new --daemon local in window-3) opens no menu on right-click either, so this is not Claude Code taking the clicks. The surface menu tests (ContextMenuTests) run against RecordingSurface, a stand-in, so nothing in the gate checks whether a real libghostty surface leaves a right-click to the host. Still to check: whether the menu opens in window-6, which the app opened at launch rather than adding later.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Cause: Appearance.swift tells every surface right-click-action = ignore (04c8fd12, 2026-09-27, from before the pane menu existed: 'a context menu Muster does not have'). In libghostty's mouseButtonCallback at the pin, .ignore falls through to 'return true', so the surface consumes every right-click and SurfaceView.rightMouseDown never reaches super, so AppKit never asks menu(for:). Only .context-menu returns false. This also explains shift-right-click over Claude Code: shift skips the mouse report, then hits the same block. Fix: right-click-action = context-menu (Ghostty's default, which selects the word under the pointer as Ghostty does), update GhosttyConfigTests, and add a real-surface test (contract tier) that a right-click over a shell opens the menu, since ContextMenuTests' RecordingSurface returns false where the real surface returned true.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-05 on 0.13.0: right-clicking inside any pane opens no menu, in every window, over a plain shell as well as over Claude Code, with or without shift. The agent row's menu in the sidebar works. So the pane menu, and Split on Machine with it, is unreachable from the mouse.

Cause: Appearance.swift tells every surface right-click-action = ignore (04c8fd12, written before the pane menu existed, on the grounds that Ghostty's right-click 'selects a word for a context menu Muster does not have'). In libghostty's mouseButtonCallback at the pin, every right-click-action except context-menu ends in 'return true', so the surface reports the press consumed, SurfaceView.rightMouseDown never calls super, and AppKit never asks menu(for:). A shift-right-click over a mouse-tracking program skips the mouse report and then lands in the same block, so the rule in docs/architecture.md that shift gets past a program cannot work either.

The gate stayed green because ContextMenuTests drive SurfaceView with RecordingSurface, which leaves the click to the host unless told otherwise; the real surface never did.

Fix:
- Appearance.swift: right-click-action = context-menu (Ghostty's default: it selects the word or link under the pointer, as Ghostty does, and returns false). Update the embedded-config comment.
- GhosttyConfigTests: the two assertions that expect ignore.
- A real-surface test in the contract tier: a right-click over a shell opens the pane menu, and a shift-right-click over a program with mouse reporting on does too.
- Check that ctrl-click still opens the menu over a shell, and that a plain right-click over a mouse-reporting program still goes to the program.
title: Right-click never opens a pane's menu: surfaces are told right-click-action = ignore
